A forgetful experience!!
Mar 2020 • Couples
Was looking for a Vietnamese restaurant to have dinner with wife on Intl Women’s Day and stumbled upon An Cafe. It is in Thao Dien Q.2 and is quite spacious inside. Great decor and ambience with lots of artefacts.

Their menu was not too expansive and a tad over priced . We ordered stir fried veggies, sea bass with coconut rice and shrimp on sugarcane skewers alongwith ginger tea. 

The tea was not fresh but made with powdered ginger/lemon grass combination and hence was not upto the mark. The coconut sauce alongwith the rice was lovely but the fish was not booked thoroughly and was unfortunately bland in taste. Shrimps on the other hand were marvellous. We asked for stir fried veggies but they came up with steamed veggies and then changed it. 

All in all am not going back. A forgetful experience. Also there is a cat roaming around asking for food (did raise its paw and asked me politely) Not a problem for me but my wife was a bit frightened.

Excellent Vietnamese Cuisine at An Cafe
Nov 2018 • Friends
I have had lunch with friends several times at An Cafe and have always found it to be a delicious and enjoyable experience. The restaurant is very attractive in a pretty, stylish rustic way and there are enough people there on a lunchtime weekend to give the place a good vibe., The staff too are super friendly and helpful. There are many tasty dishes but even the most simple - the morning glory and garlic is super fresh and of a noticeable high quality compared to this dish in other restaurants. The lemongrass beef skewers with satay sauce are particularly delicious as are the crispy spring rolls. We also tend to share a variety of salads, particularly the refreshing shredded green mango with pork and shrimps with a good addition of freshly chopped chilies. Friends that we were with have also told me that their chicken curry and chicken and ginger is very pleasant too. We usually order the garlic rice with our dishes which is like Vietnamese comfort food and another basic but favourite dish of ours. The staff are also very good at not including fish sauce if requested not to and to serve it separately. This is very important to most of our friends who cannot warm to this popular sauce at all. But unlike other restaurants who often state they have to include fish sauce, An Cafe is very accommodating. Much has been said about the food but An Cafe is also a great place to pop into for a drink , juice or coffee. A final mention must be made of teh temperature of the food here. There are many other tasty Vietnamese restaurants in town but most of them indifferently serve the food lukewarm, if that. By contrast, An Cafe's food is fresh and piping hot from the kitchen. A sheer delight.

Best Vietnamese restaurant in Thao Dien
Feb 2017 • Family
As a local person I am normally not attracted by Vietnamese restaurant that's why I passed by An cafe so many times but did not have intention to come in. Once I looked for a cafe restaurant with garden to be with my son so I chose An. I was amazed at the first sight stepped there. Immediately I felt peace by the atmosphere, byZen style decoration. I love all the corners there with the harmony between wooden tables, Buddas, green part.
They arrange tables with the distance so you can enjoy your privacy at any place you seat. Vietnamese food is delicate, good selections for vegetarians, good menu of coffee and especially Vietnamese sweet desert is amazing.
The big surprise is the price, it't cheap with the range comparing to the same level of restaurants in the area.
Staff are well trained.
Since then An has become my fav place when I want to stay with friends or family. I appreciate the love of all people who work there for the garden.
Highly recommend for everybody. You will see you will not waste any cent when you come to An.

Good food, service and prices.
Sep 2015 • Couples
I have been here twice now and am delighted to have found a more polished, but still inexpensive, restaurant for good Vietnamese food. Both times were early afternoon on the weekend.

On my first visit I had the grilled pork and spring rolls with noodles -- a standard on the street as well as many restaurants. In their case it was a great deal prettier to look at as well as being served with a filling-sized portion of pork/rolls. The sauce wasn't any different from the usual, but overall the ingredients seemed fresher and better prepared than any I've had previously. The vegetarian steamed dumplings were excellent and I'm a serious carnivore.

On the second visit I had the pork and shrimp with noodles (it's called something else on the menu; final item on the 'specials of the house'); photo included. Again, beautiful presentation and great flavor. Shrimp were cooked properly, and the size is nearly enough to stand as an entire meal -- with an appetizer or dessert I would be full.

They serve iced tea free with meals; a nice touch. Additionally, adding more protein (e.g., shrimp, pork) to your dish is possible for very little extra. If you have a big appetite I would recommend doing so. My companion's meal of stir-fried shrimp only had 3 albeit with a lot of the other ingredients [see photo].

Service was more attentive the first visit than the second. However, I have no complaints as an employee was always within sight had I needed to flag one.

Photos are of my meal, her meal, and the blended coffee, and pineapple smoothie we also had.

Bottom line: Very good Vietnamese food with excellent presentation. Pricing is also very attractive. Well worth a visit.
